summary: Objects are on a layer the drawing does not define; AUDIT creates it.
A layer uses a linetype the drawing does not define; AUDIT sets it to Continuous.
A dimension or multileader style uses a text style the drawing does not define; AUDIT sets it to Standard.
A block reference names a block the drawing does not define; AUDIT creates an empty definition.
A table entry every drawing has (layer 0, a standard style) is missing; AUDIT recreates it.
Objects use a linetype or style the drawing does not define; AUDIT sets them to the default.
A group, dimension, viewport or constraint refers to an object that does not exist; AUDIT removes the reference.
An object's geometry is invalid (zero length, no area, not a number); erasing it changes nothing on the drawing.
A block contains itself through its references; AUDIT removes the reference that closes the loop.
Two objects share one handle; AUDIT gives one of them a new handle.
The current layer, linetype or style names an entry that does not exist; AUDIT sets the default.
A polyline's vertices make a single point, so it draws nothing.
A hatch's boundary has no area, so it fills nothing.
An external reference has nothing loaded, so its drawing does not show.
An object lies far away from the rest of the drawing, so zooming to the extents shows almost nothing.
Objects are on a layer that is off or frozen, so they do not show or plot.
A text style's font is not available here, so its text is drawn with a substitute.
A text object has no text; erasing it changes nothing on the drawing.
A dimension shows fixed text instead of its measurement, so it does not follow the geometry.
One code was found more often than the check lists; the rest are counted in one diagnostic.
